### Inequality
Inequality has risen sharply across major metropolitan areas since 1980, with Gini coefficients exceeding 0.54 in several cities and income ratios reaching 18:1 between top and bottom earners [Source: ev-1].

claims.text:
### Affordability
Urban areas have experienced substantial nominal income growth, but this has not kept pace with housing costs. [Source: ev-1]
Since 2000 home prices increased by 177%, whereas median household income grew only 92% over the same period [Source: ev-1].
The Case-Shiller Index reached 325.78 in July 2024 representing a cumulative increase of 225% since January 2000 [Source: ev-1].

This divergence is particularly acute in high-cost regions; California cities exhibit price-to-income ratios between 9.6 and 12.2, which is more than double national average ratio of 4.7 [Source: ev-1].
